newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy funds flow into stocks, market seen gaining.
newsitem.headline: Italy funds flow into stocks, market seen gaining.

text.p: Italy's stock market rally in early 1997 seems set to continue after data on Thursday showed that Italian investment funds ploughed money into Italian equities last month due to potentially attractive returns, analysts said.

The Italian investment funds body Assogestioni released figures showing net funds flowed into equities for the second successive month in January, which illustrated the backing behind one of the sharpest rallies seen in Italian stocks.

The net inflow into Italian equity funds was 1.795 trillion lire ($1.1 billion) in January after December's inflow of 368 billion lire. The inflow in December was the first for two years and was a key reason for the strong early 1997 stock rally.

Italy's Mib30 blue chip index of the nation's biggest 30 listed companies rose early but then slipped on concern over an overnight Wall Street fall in the U.S., but the index has already gained nearly 19 percent so far this year.
At 1100 GMT, the Mib30 was off 1.09 percent at 18,622 and the all-share Mibtel index 0.94 percent easier at 12,517.
"A big number was expected for January so the effect on the market was limited, but we would expect the trend to continue," said Credito Italiano analyst Giordano Lombardo.

He expects some 12-13 trillion lire of funds to flow into the equity market this year and sees the BCI index testing the 900 level during the year, which is close to the record level hit in May 1986 at 908.20.
The BCI index closed on February 5 at 786.84.

Analysts pointed out investors have seen yields on domestic bonds and bank interest rates fall, and they are now looking to equities for greater potential gains, but some still remain cautious over the often-unpredictable Italian stock market.

Fund data in early January showed the first net inflow of Italian funds into equities for two years and together with falling Italian interest rates and lower bond yields helped spark an early 1997 Milan stock market rally.

Equity strategist Francesco Ricciulli at brokers Pasfin says the rally has further to go especially if the Italian government continues to show willingness to keep its finances in order for EMU entry, and also sees as positive opposition support for the government to bring its 1998 budget forward into 1997.

Overall, Assogestioni figures showed Italian investment funds had a net inflow of 18.327 trillion lire in January, compared with a net inflow of 9.177 trillion lire in December. The data showed also showed a continued flow into bonds. ($1=1,622 lire)
